title: Towards Emotion Consistency Analysis of Large Language Models in Emotional Conversational Contexts
abstract: arXiv:2605.06476v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: In this work, we conduct an analysis to examine the consistency of Large Language Models (LLMs) with respect to their own generated responses in an emotionally-driven conversational context. Specifically, the text generated by LLM is framed as a query to the same model, and its responses are subsequently assessed. This is performed with three queries across two dimensions of extreme and moderate emotions. The three queries are, in particular, false claim queries that contain inherently wrong assumptions (false presuppositions) in increasing order of intensity. Two commercial models, Claude-3.5-haiku, GPT4o-mini, and a medium-sized model, Mistral-7B, are considered in the study. translated_title: 面向情感对话情境中大语言模型情感一致性的分析研究
translated_abstract: 在本研究中，我们进行了一项分析，以检验大语言模型（LLM）在情感驱动的对话情境中相对于其自身生成回复的一致性。具体而言，将LLM生成的文本构造为对同一模型的查询，随后对其响应进行评估。这一过程在极端情感和中等情感两个维度上，通过三个查询来完成。这三个查询特别为虚假断言查询，包含按强度递增排列的固有错误假设（虚假预设）。研究中考察了两个商业模型 Claude-3.5-haiku 和 GPT4o-mini，以及一个中等规模模型 Mistral-7B。我们的研究结果表明，LLM 表现低于平均水平，且仍然容易受到查询中嵌入的错误信念的影响。这种易感性在中等情感内容上尤为显著。此外，一项基于注意力分数的扩展分析（原文截断）……
tldr: 该论文提出了一种自查询评估方法，通过将LLM自身生成的回复反馈给同一模型进行检验，发现大语言模型在情感对话情境中容易受到虚假预设的误导，且在中度情感内容下这种脆弱性尤为突出。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a self-query evaluation framework showing that LLMs remain vulnerable to false presuppositions embedded in emotional conversational contexts, with this susceptibility being especially pronounced for moderate emotional content.
